# task-03696608: colored orthogonal ray extension

## Verified recurring rule
A compact 3-cell horizontal seed of three distinct colors defines orthogonal propagation lines: extend each of its colors vertically down its seed column, while isolated markers of the same colors project horizontally along their row toward/through the seed-axis range. Preserve original markers and zero background. Infer exact stop points/intersections from the demonstrations; ray extents can be clipped by encounters with another projected feature and should not be assumed universally to reach the grid edge.

## Demo evidence
Demo 1 (15x15): top-row seed colors 6,5,3 at columns 5,6,7. Output extended color 6 down column 5, color 5 down column 6, color 3 down column 7. A separate 6 at (r4,c0) extended horizontally right through c5. A separate 3 at (r2,c14) extended horizontally left through c7. Coordinates zero-based. All other cells remained 0 except these lines and seed.

## Verified test outcome
Test (11x11) seed [4,8,5] at row 0, columns 3,4,5. 4 propagated down column 3; 8 down column 4; 5 down column 5 through row 9. Detached 4 at (r7,c0) extended horizontally through c3. Detached 5 at (r9,c10) extended horizontally left through c5. Crucial verified detail: row 10 column 5 remained 0, despite the seed 5 above; the vertical 5 ray ended at row 9, where the detached 5 horizontal ray met it. Submission was correct.

## Practical method / cautions
1. Identify the distinct-color horizontal seed, typically three adjacent cells.
2. Project seed colors vertically and identify detached markers of those colors projecting horizontally toward the seed columns.
3. Preserve zeros outside the rays and preserve all initial markers.
4. Pay attention to collisions/endpoints: the verified test's vertical 5 ended at the row of the matching detached horizontal 5; do not blindly fill the entire column to the boundary. Use demos to determine clipping semantics on each recurrence."
}
